To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the chiral quarks, which are constituents of a nucleon at low normalization scale, are not valence quarks, but have a large antiquark component.

the quark--antiquark asymmetry in the proton is large, that the antiquark distributions are sizable, that the antiquarks are dominantly valence, and that there are more antiquarks than quarks in the proton.
the isosinglet antiquark distributions in the nucleon at a low scale, obtained in a self-consistent calculation, exhibit a large number of antiquarks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure of the nucleon, the pion and the kaon in the framework of the effective choral theory.
the calculation of parton distribution functions (pdfs) in the framework of the chiral quarksoliton model (CQSM), which is an effective field theory for baryons in the large--Nc limit.
the calculation of the parton distribution functions of the nucleon in the chiral constituent quark model.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the antiquark distributions are not suppressed compared to the quark distributions, even though the quark distribution at the same low scale is dominated by the constituent quark.
